_README: SHARADAR SF1 -> the repo's `fundamentals_history` vocabulary. The map is DATA, not code:
`field_map.py` reads it and is fully deterministic given this file (D22's governance,
applied to the map as well as to the registers).
`columns` must cover EVERY name in `HISTORY_STATEMENT_ORDER` (kpi_catalogue.py) -- the
loader fails loudly on a gap, and on a `from` that is not in `SHARADAR_SF1_COLUMNS`.
FOUR KINDS, a closed vocabulary:
"direct"  -- rename a Sharadar column. Optional `negate` and `split_basis`.
"derived" -- computed from OTHER MAPPED COLUMNS by a named `op`, on the TTM frame.
"sec"     -- no Sharadar source; the SEC layer owns it (D18). NaN until phase 4 merges.
"null"    -- no source anywhere. The column is kept because the contract asserts by
list equality, and documented as a free loss.
`negate: "if_non_positive"` flips the sign where Sharadar's convention holds and NULLs
the cells where it does not. NEVER `true`: 13 of 1,346 stored rows carry a POSITIVE
`capex`, and an unconditional flip writes a negative into a `non_negative` column.
`split_basis` de-adjusts Sharadar's RETROACTIVE SPLIT ADJUSTMENT, using the split events
in `sharadar_actions`. `"count"` divides by the forward-split factor, `"per_share"`
multiplies. See `_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENT` below -- this is wider than phase 2 reported.
`op` is a CLOSED vocabulary (`sum`, `ratio`, `ratio_minus_one`). `formula` beside it is
PROSE FOR A READER and is asserted against `inputs`/`op` by the loader, so the two can
never drift. An eval-able expression string would be code in a config file.
EVERY derived formula is evaluated on the TTM FRAME, after `build_ttm`, exactly as the SEC
path's `_FORMULAS` are. A ratio of two TTM levels is not the TTM of a ratio, and this is
the basis decision (#31) the repo already made.
Keys starting with _ are documentation and must be skipped by the reader.
generated: 2026-08-26
_BASIS_FORKS: Known, DECIDED, and recorded here so the next reader does not 'fix' them:
totalRevenue <- revenue        the filer's OWN caption. JPM matches the SEC layer exactly;
AXP is 6.6-8.1% low (post-provision). Adjudicated PER TICKER
in phase 4's override register, NOT here.
accountsReceivable <- receivables   trade AND non-trade; the repo's SEC column is
`AccountsReceivableNetCurrent`. Affects dso,
cash_conversion_cycle and Beneish DSRI.
accountsPayable <- payables    trade AND non-trade. Affects dpo.
ppeNet <- ppnenet              INCLUDES operating ROU assets; the SEC path SUBTRACTS
finance-lease ROU where the linkbase declares it.
shortTermDebt <- debtc         lease-INCLUSIVE; the SEC column is lease-exclusive.
longTermDebt <- debtnc         lease-INCLUSIVE, same fork.
totalDebt <- debt              both lease-inclusive. This one genuinely AGREES.
pretaxIncome <- ebt            Sharadar tags `ebt` as [Metrics], not [Income Statement].
netIncome <- consolinc         NOT `netinc`. Measured on JPM's 11 overlap dates: the repo's
netIncome equals `consolinc` on all 11 and differs from
`netinc` on all 11. `consolinc` includes NCI, the repo basis.
cash = cashneq + investmentsc  the repo's widening, best available. Restricted cash is
absent from SF1 and that loss is accepted.
ebitda = opinc + depamor       TOP-DOWN. NEVER Sharadar's `ebitda`, which is bottom-up
(netinc + taxexp + intexp + depamor) and therefore carries
every non-operating item.
debtToEquity = debt / equity   NEVER Sharadar's `de`, which is LIABILITIES/equity despite
being named 'Debt to Equity Ratio'.
profitMargins                  NEVER Sharadar's `netmargin`, which is on the `netinccmn`
basis (after preferred) -- a different numerator.
epsDiluted                     ⚠ DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, measured. The plan mapped this
DIRECT from `epsdil`. `epsdil` is on the `netinccmn` basis:
over 549 ARQ rows it matches netinccmn/shareswadil on 426,
`netinc` on 412 and `consolinc` on only 296 -- and
`netinccmn != consolinc` on 208 of the 549 (38%). Mapping it
direct would put a netinccmn-based EPS in the same row as a
consolinc-based netIncome. Derived from the repo's own two
columns instead, exactly as the SEC path does.
_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENT: ⚠ THE FEATURE COLUMNS ARE ON THE VENDOR'S SPLIT-ADJUSTED BASIS, DELIBERATELY. Only
`sharesOutstandingPit` is de-adjusted, and it exists for OWNERSHIP RATIOS ALONE.
THE CANCELLATION IDENTITY -- why de-adjusting the feature columns was wrong:
Sharadar sharesbas(d)   = real_shares(d) x F(d)   (vendor back-fills to today's basis)
Yahoo    close_split(d) = raw_price(d)   / F(d)   (vendor restates to today's basis)
close_split x sharesbas = raw_price x real_shares   <- F(d) cancels IDENTICALLY
So on the split-adjusted basis market cap is correct with NO split event list at all, and
correctness stops depending on a feed that will never be complete. Verified: AAPL
WHAT DE-ADJUSTING THE FEATURE COLUMNS COST, measured 2026-09-01 on 51,255 rows:
* `sharesOutstanding = sharesbas / F(d)` made market cap a FUNCTION of the event list,
and that list has nine holes -- so AAPL was de-adjusted and GOOGL was not, and ONE
COLUMN SAT ON DIFFERENT BASES FOR DIFFERENT TICKERS IN THE SAME CROSS-SECTION. For a
cross-sectional long/short that is the worst possible failure: it corrupts the
RANKING, not just a level. ANET was worse still -- PARTIALLY de-adjusted (2021
applied, 2024 missing), so its residual factor was neither the point-in-time count
nor the vendor's.
* 10,996 of 51,255 rows (21.5%) across 277 tickers were de-adjusted DOWN and 601 UP
(reverse splits -- GE x8, C x10, AIG x20, TMUS x2 -- giving mcap overstated 8-20x).
* It made the share-change features outright wrong: a 4:1 split read as +300% issuance
in the quarter the factor stepped, hitting `shares_growth`, `diluted_shares_growth`,
`buyback_yield`/`shareholder_yield` and one of nine Piotroski legs. On the vendor
basis both legs carry the same restatement, so shares(t)/shares(t-1) = 1 through a
split and all four become correct with no code change.
* `split_part < 1` is definitionally 'this stock splits LATER' -- strictly future
information in the mcap denominator of 21.5% of rows, and those rows earned 27.81%
forward 12m against 15.38% for everything else. +12.4pp/yr of pure look-ahead.
THE VENDOR ADJUSTMENT IS REAL -- this is not a claim that Sharadar is unadjusted. SF1
reports a pre-split quarter on the POST-split basis across its whole share block:
`sharesbas`, `shareswa`, `shareswadil`, `eps`, `epsdil` and `dps`. `sharefactor` is 1.0
on every affected row and does NOT flag it. Measured, as-filed (SEC cover page) vs stored:
NVDA 2022-03-18  shareswadil (ART) 25,350,000,000 -> /10 == SEC dilutedShares exactly
WMT  10 of 10 pre-split rows: sharesbas/3 == SEC sharesOutstanding EXACTLY
AMZN 2021-10-29  sharesbas 10,142,952,400 against ~507m then outstanding (20-for-1,
That adjustment is exactly what makes the basis CONSISTENT with `close_split`, which is
why the four feature columns now keep it and only the PIT twin undoes it.
`sharesOutstandingPit` = sharesbas / F(d), where F(d) is the product of every genuine
split dated AFTER the row's own filing date. Its ONLY consumers are `inst_ownership_pct`
and the insider %-of-shares leg -- both divide an as-filed 13F / Form-4 share count by a
share count, so both legs must be as-filed. `basicShares` / `dilutedShares` feed
per-share ratios where the factor cancels, and a PIT `dividendsPerShare` has no consumer.
THE EVENT LIST is the UNION of `sharadar_actions` and yfinance (`prices_splits`), under
the corroboration rule in `field_map.split_events`. Sharadar alone misses GOOGL 2022 x20,
NVDA 2021 x4, TSLA 2022 x3, AVGO/CMG/ANET 2024, BKNG/MNST/AMCR 2026, and carries at least
one false positive (SJM 2002-05-30 x0.945, a merger share-issuance factor).
⚠ THE HON TRAP -- a `split` row is NOT always a share split, and it still applies to
`sharesOutstandingPit`. HON's 0.5 is dated 2026-06-29 and CO-DATED with `spinoff=1` /
`spinoffdividend=221.01` (Honeywell Aerospace): it is the spinoff's PRICE adjustment, not
a share-count event. HON's own as-filed cover page proves it -- `sharesbas` reads
Applying it would have DOUBLED every HON share count in the history. So a split candidate
is USED only when no `spinoff` row shares its (ticker, date).
_ADDED_COLUMNS_README: second half: one basis per column, so parent-only and parent-plus-NCI are two columns and
never one column that changes meaning. Its NCI leg is SEC-owned, so it is populated for
the 54-ticker SEC roster only -- which is exactly why it is a second column.
`employees` and `regime` are the other two SEC-owned columns that are not in the 60
(D18/D18b). `regime` is the FILING'S RESOLUTION REGIME, stamped per filing by the SEC facts
layer. ⚠ It is NOT derived from GICS via `sp500_tickers`: that would silently change what
the column MEANS, from 'how this filing's KPIs were resolved' to 'what sector this company
is in'. Those are different facts that happen to correlate.
⚠ `regime` is the only NON-FLOAT column in the contract (a label, not a value). Phase 3
emits it as NaN like every other `sec` column; phase 4 fills it as TEXT.
_EXTRAS_README: Sharadar columns with NO repo counterpart (D16). These revive eight currently-dead cube
KEYED BY THE VENDOR COLUMN, EMITTED UNDER `to`. D16 says to keep Sharadar's own name where
there is nothing to rename to, and that was first read as keeping its own SPELLING -- which
put `ncfx`, `prefdivis` and `accoci` in a table whose other 63 columns are camelCase. `to`
is now REQUIRED and the loader refuses one that collides with a contract column, because two
sources writing one column would let the later one win silently. The vendor spelling stays
the KEY, so this file still reads as a map FROM `fundamentals_sharadar`.
`basis` drives `build_ttm`: `duration` is summed over four discrete quarters, `instant`
takes the period-end value. It is declared HERE rather than read off `SHARADAR_FLOW_FIELDS`
because that constant was written for the phase-2 diagnostic and deliberately excludes
per-share figures from its flow set -- `dps` IS additive across quarters (12 months of
dividends per share), a weighted-average share count is not.
`cashneq` is carried as an extra although the plan did not list it: the repo's `cash` is a
WIDER concept (cash + restricted + short-term investments), so the narrow line has no repo
counterpart, and carrying it lets `cash` be a plain TTM-frame formula instead of needing a
second evaluation space in this file.

TAUTOLOGY that holds on 598 of 598 ARQ rows and proves nothing about
